purpose: This medication is used to lower very high triglyceride levels in your blood. High triglycerides can increase your risk of heart disease and inflammation of the pancreas. It is usually used along with a healthy diet and exercise.
how_it_works: Omega-3-acid ethyl esters are a purified, concentrated form of fish oil containing healthy fatty acids called EPA and DHA. These fatty acids work in your liver to slow down the production of triglycerides and help your body clear them from your blood more efficiently. Think of it as helping your liver do a better job of managing fats in your bloodstream.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include a fishy taste or burping, upset stomach, nausea, diarrhea, and back pain. Some people also notice a mild skin rash or flushing. Taking it with food can help reduce stomach-related side effects.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to fish or shellfish before taking this medication. It may slightly increase your LDL ('bad') cholesterol in some people, so your doctor will monitor your blood levels. This medication can affect blood clotting, so let your doctor know if you take blood thinners like warfarin. Avoid drinking too much alcohol, as it can also raise your triglycerides and reduce the effectiveness of this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 4 grams per day, either taken all at once or split into two 2-gram doses with meals. Your doctor will tell you the exact dose that is right for you based on your triglyceride levels.
